systemPromptSection: pluglet is the user's task list: a JSON file on disk that the user also reads and writes through the `pluglet` CLI, so what you add is visible to them and what they add is visible to you. Use the pluglet_* tools whenever the user asks to record, review or count their tasks, or asks which pluglet commands their configuration offers. Pass the same `config` value on every call in a conversation so every call addresses one task file. Only add, list and help are callable here: a task cannot be completed or deleted through these tools, and a command that pluglet_help reports but these tools do not cover is something the user runs themselves.

tools.name: pluglet_add
tools.description: Append a new, not-done task to the task list and return `added <id>: <title>`, where id is the next sequential integer.

config.description: Path to the pluglet config file; relative paths resolve from the working directory. Omit it to use `pluglet.json` there.

tools.name: pluglet_list
tools.description: Return every task in id order, one per line as `<id> [x] <title>` for a done task and `<id> [ ] <title>` for an open one. Empty output means the list has no tasks.

config.description: Path to the pluglet config file; relative paths resolve from the working directory. Omit it to use `pluglet.json` there.

tools.name: pluglet_help
tools.description: Return the commands available under the config, one per line as `<name>  <description>`, including the commands that the config's plugins add.

config.description: Path to the pluglet config file; relative paths resolve from the working directory. Omit it to use `pluglet.json` there.
